name: LOWER STREET
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE STREET
LOOK_AT: Main Street's mud, continued. Out here it has stopped trying to impress anyone.
Wheel ruts, swinging wide around the corner. Every wagon in town takes it the long way, out of respect.
The far end of town. In Providence this is where the better houses would be. Here it is where the street gives up and becomes a road.
LISTEN_TO: Quieter than Main Street. The piano is a rumor from here.
Hooves in the livery, and the mud settling after them.
A dog, two streets over, objecting to something on principle.

overrides.PICK_UP: Lower Street's mud is Main Street's, only less looked at. I'll leave it its privacy.

subjects.name: SUMP'S WINDOW
LOOK_AT: The Claims Registrar's window, lit! Behind the glare is a man who has never once been surprised. I mean to be the first to surprise him.
Lamplight through old glass, gone wavy with age. Even the window has been made to wait.
The lamp is always lit. I have never seen anyone trim it. I suspect it is filed.
LISTEN_TO: A pen, scratching, then a long pause, then a stamp. The rhythm of a form being found incomplete.
A page turning, very slowly. Somewhere in there a claim is being read to the last comma.
The stamp again. It is the most decisive sound in Consolation.

overrides.OPEN: It doesn't open. The Registrar's business is done through the door, in the order received.

subjects.name: THE CHURCH
LOOK_AT: The church, which on weekdays is the meeting hall and on most days is neither. The whitest thing in town, because it is the only thing anyone repaints.
The steps up to the doors. One has been replaced; the rest have been worn smooth by people arriving in a hurry and leaving slowly.
The belfry has a bell of its own, rung from inside on a rope. Out here the ringing is done by hand, from the post, at whatever hour the ringer feels it.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing from inside. The pews are holding their breath for Sunday.
The doors, ticking as the night cools them. Even the church settles.
Somewhere inside, a hymnal falling shut. Nobody there to have been reading it.

overrides.TALK_TO: I said a short word for my claim. It was received the way the Registrar receives things: in silence, and filed.

subjects.name: THE BELL
LOOK_AT: A bell on a post by the church steps, with a dent where the mallet lands. It was cast to a note, and it has been coming down off it ever since.
Brass, gone green at the rim. Somebody polishes the dent and nothing else.
You can't tune a bell, not properly. I could still have a long talk with it.
LISTEN_TO: It hums when the wind catches it. Even humming, it's low.
I flicked it with a fingernail. Half a step flat, and comfortable there.
Nothing now. It's resting between insults to the scale.

overrides.TALK_TO: I told it it was flat. It took it better than most of the people I've told things to here.
overrides.USE: Not without the mallet, and not without the man who owns the mallet, and ideally not at all.

subjects.name: THE LIVERY
LOOK_AT: The livery stable. The doors stand open on a lantern and a heap of hay. The horses are further in, out of sight and, from the sound of them, out of patience.
A hay loft over the doors, shut tight, as though the hay might make a run for it.
I could hire a horse, if I had the price of a horse's afternoon. I have about the price of its nap.
LISTEN_TO: Horses, shifting their weight and their opinions.
A long, judgmental snort. I'm choosing to believe it was aimed at the street in general.
A bucket set down, and a horse investigating it.

subjects.name: THE TROUGH
LOOK_AT: A water trough with a skin of dust on it and a square of night sky in the middle.
Horses drink from it, dogs drink from it, and one man, I suspect, late on Saturdays.
Planks, pitch and iron bands. It holds water the way this town holds a grudge: completely.
LISTEN_TO: A slow drip from the seam, keeping its own time.
Nothing. Still water, minding its business.
A moth on the surface, rowing for shore.

overrides.USE: I washed my face in it. Now I'm dusty and wet, which out here passes for clean.

THE BELL-RINGER.PICK_UP: I am not going to pick up the bell-ringer. He is the only thing holding the bell up, morally.
THE BELL-RINGER.PUSH: He sways enough on his own. I'm not going to add a vote.
THE BELL-RINGER.USE: He has one use, and he is already putting it to work, half a step flat.
